A1.justification: Both PDFs describe DimABSA, with matching scientific sections, equations, experiments and appendices. However, missing Japanese and Cyrillic glyphs in v1 Appendix A, and clipping of some v3 example outputs, limit exact comparison of those examples. The remaining material supports reliable comparison.

before.justification: V1 reports original annotation-agreement measurements, LLM benchmark results, few-shot analyses and categorical sentiment evaluations in Tables 2–3 and the appendices.

after.justification: V3 retains original dataset analyses and experimental results in Tables 2–3 and Appendices G–J.

M1.justification: The annotation pipeline, three dimensional tasks, prompting procedures and QLoRA fine-tuning approach are retained. The relocated prompts remain substantively identical; terminology changes do not establish a new method.

E1.justification: Both versions cover the same ten language-domain datasets across six languages and four domains, with the same dimensional and categorical tasks. The categorical dataset's newly supplied access link does not introduce new evaluation coverage.

E2.justification: The same six LLMs participate in corresponding comparisons. V1's 'Mistral-3 14B' already links to Ministral-3-14B-Reasoning-2512 in Appendix C, establishing that v3's corrected name does not identify an added comparator.

E3.justification: The dataset splits, first-k demonstration selection, shot counts, metrics and fine-tuning settings match. V1 Appendix C already specifies the learning rate, batch size, five epochs and H200 hardware moved into v3 Section 4.1. Omitted scoring instructions reduce documentation but do not establish a changed experimental procedure.

E4.justification: The category-distribution analyses, few-shot sensitivity curves, VA-distribution comparisons and dimensional-versus-categorical evaluations are retained. Reordered appendices and redrawn plots do not introduce additional analyses.

E5.justification: Five-annotator aggregation, the 1.5-standard-deviation outlier filter, agreement measurements and descriptive standard deviations remain unchanged. Neither version adds model-run uncertainty, seed information, confidence intervals or significance tests.

E6.justification: Appendix G corrects GPT-5 mini's zero-shot DimASQP average cF1 from 0.2540 to 0.2254 and Kimi K2 Thinking's one-shot average cPrecision from 0.2540 to 0.2640. Categorical ASC average precision for Llama-3.3 changes from 0.8308 to 0.6308. The zho-lap positive percentage also changes from 71.03% to 71.04% despite unchanged counts. Main Table 3 remains unchanged.

T1.justification: Equations 1–3 retain the same VA-RMSE, continuous true-positive and normalized-distance definitions. The cF1 construction and worked example are mathematically unchanged; notation edits introduce no new formal result.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction add the claim that DimABSA was publicly released and used for SemEval-2026 Task 3 Track A, attracting over 300 participants. The central dataset, three-task and cF1 contributions, and benchmark-difficulty claims, remain unchanged.

C2.justification: Section 2.1 expands the rationale and qualifications for translated language coverage. The Limitations section adds concrete explanations involving culturally different scale-use patterns and emotional expressiveness. Existing interpretations of model performance and few-shot calibration remain stable.

D1.justification: V3 reports public release and provides access links for the dimensional and categorical datasets. Existing implementation settings and model links are relocated rather than newly disclosed. Conversely, v3 Appendix F omits v1 Appendix E's explicit two-decimal rounding and out-of-range prediction invalidation instructions.

R1.justification: V3 adds Hipson and Mohammad (2021), Teodorescu et al. (2023), and Yu et al. (2026), extending the application context and documenting SemEval positioning. The claimed relationship to earlier ABSA datasets and the multilingual novelty claim remain unchanged.

P1.justification: V3 makes localized prose, terminology, author-name and affiliation corrections, renames Discussion to Analysis, and reorganizes the appendices. Implementation details move into Section 4.1 and prompting instructions become separate appendices. The main narrative structure remains intact.

P2.justification: V3 relocates Figure 1, redraws Figure 4 with adjusted legends, and rearranges appendix displays to eliminate heading-only pages. Appendix A renders previously missing multilingual text, although some output strings are clipped. Most figures and table structures are retained.

improvement.justification: Corrected appendix averages, documented dataset access, more readable multilingual examples and clearer cultural limitations improve usability and reporting. The main scientific evidence remains stable. These gains outweigh limited drawbacks: omitted scoring instructions, remaining example clipping, and the new zho-lap percentage inconsistency, where the displayed counts support 71.03%, not 71.04%.
